clientID.description: Audience the cluster's apiserver accepts in the person's id_token; empty is the first of `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences`, the cross-client audience muster requests at login. Both empty: created clusters trust no identity provider.

groupsClaim.description: id_token claim the cluster's apiserver takes as the groups.

usernameClaim.description: id_token claim the cluster's apiserver takes as the username.

tenantServiceAccount.description: ServiceAccount in every org namespace the installation's Flux runs a composed release under when the release's objects live in that namespace: the pool release (its Cluster API objects) and the `<cluster>-agent-platform` slice release (its child HelmReleases). Giant Swarm installations enforce the `flux-multi-tenancy` policy on every HelmRelease in `org-<org>` — a `serviceAccountName` or a kubeconfig on each —, and `automation` is the org's tenant ServiceAccount there. A release installing into a cluster (the `<cluster>-gpu-operator` release, the slice's children) is delivered through the cluster's `<cluster>-kubeconfig` Secret instead, the installation's own cluster included. Empty renders none, for a lab without the policy.

fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully qualified app name.

apiURL.description: GitHub's REST API, for `GET /user` and the pull request.

enabled.description: Offer commit mode (`mode: commit` on `create_cluster`, `delete_cluster`, `create_node_pool` and `delete_node_pool`: the pull request opened as the person in the repository that owns the cluster). Needs `oauth.enabled` and `tokenExchange.tokenEndpoint`: muster keeps forwarding the person's ID token as the bearer (`muster.mcpServer.auth.forwardToken`) and the server fetches the person's GitHub App user token for each commit (RFC 8693). Off: commit mode is refused.

audience.description: RFC 8693 audience: the App whose grant the broker releases. Also the App named in `grant_required` answers and listed under the MCPServer's `auth.providerApps`, so muster answers with that App's sign-in link. The App needs contents and pull-request write on every repository a commit targets. Required with `tokenEndpoint`.

caSecretName.description: Optional existing Secret with `ca.crt` for the broker's private CA.

clientID.description: Confidential broker client ID. Empty: read from the Secret's `client-id` key.

clientSecret.description: Confidential broker client secret; the chart renders it into a Secret. Prefer `existingSecret`, which wins when both are set.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret in the release namespace with `client-secret` (and `client-id` when `clientID` is empty).

tokenEndpoint.description: RFC 8693 token endpoint (muster's broker) that releases the person's GitHub App user token for a commit. Set: only a commit asks for GitHub, and one without the person's grant answers `grant_required` naming `audience`. Needs `github.enabled`, `oauth.enabled` with Dex, `oauth.downstream.enabled` and `muster.mcpServer.auth.forwardToken`; required with `github.enabled`.

global.description: Platform-wide values a parent chart (the `agent-platform` meta chart) shares with every component; Helm forwards them to this chart. `oauth.*` reads the identity contract as its defaults: `global.identity.issuerUrl`, `global.identity.clientId`, `global.identity.existingSecret`, `global.identity.ca.secretName` / `.key`, and `global.domain` for the OAuth base URL. Empty here; a chart installed on its own sets `oauth.*` directly.

dcgmExporter.description: Run NVIDIA's DCGM exporter on the GPU pools' nodes through the composed `<cluster>-gpu-operator` release (its `dcgmExporter.enabled`), for an installation whose observability scrapes it (a ServiceMonitor on the `nvidia-dcgm-exporter` Service in `kube-system`). Off by default: nothing scrapes the exporter out of the box, and on a fresh pool node it is an image pull and a pod initialising DCGM on the GPU while the device plugin brings `nvidia.com/gpu` up.

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart appVersion.

name.description: Name of the installation. `list_clusters` reports the Cluster of that name as the installation's own cluster (its management cluster); empty marks none.

enabled.description: Serve the MCP streamable-HTTP endpoint (the server's only surface).

namespace.description: Namespace model-manager runs in on the installation. `create_node_pool` registers each serving cluster's kserve backend there by writing its ConfigMap of model-manager's runtime-registration contract (`model-backend-kserve` for the installation's own cluster, `model-backend-kserve-<cluster>` for a workload cluster); `delete_node_pool` of the cluster's last pool removes that cluster's; `enable_model_serving` and `disable_model_serving` register and remove it too.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to this server; rendered only with `oauth.enabled`. `forwardToken` makes muster forward the session's IdP id_token byte-identical (the SSO path this chart trusts through its trusted audiences). `requiredAudiences` are extra audiences that token must carry — the Dex cross-client audience the kube-apiserver trusts (`dex-k8s-authenticator` on Giant Swarm clusters; agentlab's is `kubernetes`) so `oauth.downstream` works; muster requests them at login, so users re-login after a change. They are trusted as bearer audiences by construction, since the server's trusted audiences are `oauth.trustedAudiences` plus this list. A Google IdP has no cross-client audiences: leave the list empty.

autoStart.description: Start the server connection when muster initializes.

displayName.description: Human-friendly name the Dev Portal shows for this server, rendered as the `ui.giantswarm.io/display-name` annotation. Empty renders none.

enabled.description: Register this server with muster by rendering an `mcpservers.muster.giantswarm.io` CR in the release namespace. Tools then appear as `x_<name>_<tool>`.

labels.description: Extra labels on the MCPServer CR.

name.description: MCPServer CR name (drives the tool prefix).

allowPublicClientRegistration.description: Deprecated, removed in a later release: accept dynamic client registration without an initial access token, public clients included (labs only). MCP clients register with client ID metadata documents.

enabled.description: Accept URL client IDs (client ID metadata documents) (`OAUTH_ENABLE_CLIENT_ID_METADATA_DOCUMENTS`).

Serve RFC 7591 dynamic client registration (`OAUTH_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_CLIENT_REGISTRATION`). MCP 2026-07-28 deprecates it in favour of client ID metadata documents; it stays on for clients that still register this way.

secretKeyRef.description: Secret key with the RFC 7591 initial access token a registration must present (mcp-oauth reads it from `OAUTH_INITIAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE`).

enabled.description: Run the authorization server. Off makes cluster-manager a resource server only (`OAUTH_ENABLE_AUTHORIZATION_SERVER=false`).

issuer.description: Public base URL of this server, the issuer of its tokens and metadata (`OAUTH_ISSUER`; https, or http on loopback). Empty uses the deprecated `oauth.baseURL`, else `https://<fullname>.<global.domain>`.

type.description: Token storage (`OAUTH_STORAGE_BACKEND`). Memory loses every session on restart and needs one replica.
The OpenID Provider people sign in with: `dex` or `google` (`OAUTH_PROVIDER`). Empty uses the deprecated `oauth.provider`, else `dex`.

secretKeyRef.description: Secret key with the CA of a Dex that serves a private certificate (`OAUTH_DEX_CA_FILE`). Empty name uses the deprecated `oauth.dex.caSecret`, else `global.identity.ca`.

id.description: OAuth client ID at the provider. Empty uses the deprecated `oauth.dex.clientID` or `oauth.google.clientID`, else `global.identity.clientId` (dex).

secretKeyRef.description: Secret key with the client secret, mounted as a file. Empty name uses the deprecated `oauth.existingSecret`, else `global.identity.existingSecret`, else a Secret from the deprecated inline client secret.

issuer.description: Dex issuer URL. Empty uses the deprecated `oauth.dex.issuerURL`, else `global.identity.issuerUrl`.

allowPrivateURLs.description: Deprecated, no effect, not passed to the server: the Dex client reaches private addresses and follows HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY without it. Remove it from your values; the key goes away in a later release.

enabled.description: Call the Kubernetes API as the caller: everything a request does presents the caller's IdP token, so the caller's RBAC governs — the apiserver must trust the IdP and the token's audience (a Dex install lists that audience in `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences`; a Google install's client id is the apiserver's `--oidc-client-id`). This is cluster-manager's rule (every write as the person), so it is on by default and takes effect with `oauth.enabled`. The ServiceAccount then holds no permissions: the chart renders no RBAC for it (`rbac.create` is moot).

Make cluster-manager an OAuth 2.1 resource server (mcp-oauth): the MCP endpoint requires a bearer token, and every call carries the caller's identity. On the Agent Platform muster forwards the session's IdP ID token to this server (MCPServer `auth.forwardToken`, rendered below) and the portal's calls arrive the same way through muster; both are accepted from the provider people sign in with (`resourceServer.trustedIssuers`). Off: anonymous, acting as the ServiceAccount, only for a server nothing but a trusted proxy can reach.

existingSecret.description: Deprecated: use `authorizationServer.upstream.client.secretKeyRef`. Existing Secret with `dex-client-secret` (dex) or `google-client-secret` (+ optional `google-client-id`) (google).

clientID.description: Deprecated: use `authorizationServer.upstream.client.id`. Empty reads the Secret key `google-client-id`.

additionalResources.description: Further protected resources on the same origin, each by its full URL (`OAUTH_ADDITIONAL_RESOURCES`). The MCP endpoint is always a protected resource.

authorizationServers.description: Issuer identifiers the resource metadata advertises (`OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_SERVERS`, RFC 9728 `authorization_servers`): this server's issuer or a trusted issuer. Empty advertises this server's issuer; required with `authorizationServer.enabled` false, since MCP clients find the authorization server here.

requireResourceAccessTokens.description: Accept only tokens whose audience names this server's resource (`OAUTH_REQUIRE_RESOURCE_ACCESS_TOKENS`), as MCP requires. Off while the platform forwards ID tokens (giantswarm/giantswarm#39102).

resource.description: The main protected resource, by its full URL (`OAUTH_RESOURCE`). Empty uses the issuer.

trustedIssuers.description: The issuers whose JWTs are accepted (`OAUTH_TRUSTED_ISSUERS`). A trust anchor: set it only from the release's own values or a GitOps-managed ConfigMap that only installation administrators write. Each entry: `issuer`, `jwksURI` and `audiences` (required), `subjectClaim` (`sub` or `email`), `acceptedTypHeaders`, `allowedClaims`, `allowPrivateIPJWKSHosts`, `openIDProvider` (true for the provider people sign in with, whose bearers are their ID tokens), and `certificateAuthority` with a `secretKeyRef` or `configMapKeyRef` (`name`, `key`). Empty trusts the provider people sign in with (`authorizationServer.upstream`) as `openIDProvider`: its ID tokens are accepted as bearer tokens, a deviation from MCP's audience rule until per-backend tokens (ID-JAG, giantswarm/giantswarm#39102). They are accepted for the client people sign in with (`authorizationServer.upstream.client.id`, or the deprecated `oauth.trustedAudiences`) and `muster.mcpServer.auth.requiredAudiences`, in that order and without duplicates.

allowPrivateIPJWKSHosts.description: Deprecated: list the provider in `resourceServer.trustedIssuers` with these `allowPrivateIPJWKSHosts`. Hosts, other than the issuer's own, whose JWKS may resolve to an RFC 1918 or RFC 4193 address.

allowPrivateIPs.description: Deprecated, no effect, not passed to the server: the issuer host of the configured provider may resolve to a private address for its JWKS without it; list any other JWKS host in allowPrivateIPJWKSHosts. Remove it from your values; the key goes away in a later release.

trustedAudiences.description: Deprecated: list the provider in `resourceServer.trustedIssuers` with these `audiences`. The OAuth client IDs whose ID tokens of the provider people sign in with are accepted.

enabled.description: Serve Prometheus metrics on `GET /metrics` of the `metrics` port: `mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds` per tool, and `http_server_request_duration_seconds` for the REST API and the MCP endpoint. Off, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none`: nothing is served, and nothing is pushed to `observability.otel.endpoint` either.

port.description: Port of the metrics listener, apart from the API port so an HTTPRoute or the OAuth guard never covers it.

endpoint.description: OTLP collector the server exports its traces to (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`), e.g. `http://otlp-gateway.kube-system.svc:4317` for gRPC. Empty exports nothing; the W3C propagator still honours an inbound `traceparent`.

headers.description: Extra OTLP headers as `key=value,...` (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`), e.g. `X-Scope-OrgID=giantswarm` for the collector's tenant.

resourceAttributes.description: Extra resource attributes as `key=value,...`, appended to the pod's `k8s.pod.name`, `k8s.namespace.name` and `k8s.node.name` (`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`).

sampler.description: Trace sampler (`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`). Parent-based: a call arriving with a sampled `traceparent` (muster's) is always kept, a root span is sampled at `samplerArg`.

samplerArg.description: Sampler argument (`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`): the ratio of root spans kept.

create.description: Create the read-only ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding (Cluster API clusters, machine pools, control planes and infrastructure, Flux HelmReleases, Giant Swarm Releases) — the ServiceAccount's own permissions for a release without OAuth. Ignored with `oauth.enabled` and `oauth.downstream.enabled`: the ServiceAccount then gets no RBAC at all.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas. The server holds no state; more than one is fine.

resources.description: Container resources. ephemeral-storage covers the `tmp` emptyDir mounted at /tmp, which holds only the Go runtime's scratch files.

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Old ReplicaSets the Deployment keeps. Kubernetes defaults to 10; fewer keeps stale pod templates out of the PolicyReport.

enabled.description: Render a ServiceMonitor for the `metrics` port. Also needs `observability.metrics.enabled`; the meta chart turns this on with the tenant label.

interval.description: Scrape interval; empty uses the Prometheus Operator default.

labels.description: Labels on the ServiceMonitor, beside the chart's own. The Giant Swarm observability platform routes a scrape to a Mimir tenant by `observability.giantswarm.io/tenant`; a monitor without it writes to no tenant.

cacheClaim.description: Base name of the model cache `PersistentVolumeClaim`s in the serving namespace (the connectivity chart's default `modelServing.cache.pvc.name`). A claim outlives the pool and is one volume bound in one zone, so the cache is one claim per zone: `create_node_pool` with `zones` composes the zone's claim into the pool's slice — the claim Bound there, else `<cacheClaim>-<zone>` — and pins the pool's nodes to the zone (the gpu-node-pool chart's `pool.zones`); `list_clusters` names every claim with its zone under serving readiness.

certificateIssuer.description: cert-manager `ClusterIssuer` the `<cluster>-agent-platform` slice release asks for the certificate of `models.<domain>` when the platform's wildcard is not usable: on a workload cluster (another domain) and on the installation's own cluster when the platform's release names no `gatewayApi.gateway.tls.secretName` (TLS terminated at the fleet's edge Gateway, its wildcard in another namespace). `letsencrypt-giantswarm` is the issuer every Giant Swarm cluster runs. Empty composes none — the connectivity chart then refuses a models Gateway without a certificate.

namespace.description: Namespace on a serving cluster where the LLMInferenceServices go, named as `target.servingNamespace` in the registered `kserve` backend.

sliceChartVersion.description: Exact `agent-platform` chart version the `<cluster>-agent-platform` slice release pins. Empty follows the chart from the version the installation's own platform release runs (at least 4.85.0, the first chart that names a targeted release's children per target) to the next major; set it only for a lab running an unreleased chart.

sizeLimit.description: Size limit of the `tmp` emptyDir mounted at /tmp; the kubelet evicts the pod when the volume grows past it. Empty sets no limit.
